The polar curve $r=9$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. The Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(r,\theta )=(9,\frac{3\pi }{4}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $P$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =9cos\,(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =9\cdot -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =9sin\,(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =9\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2},\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}).$
